implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 and standards STD-02.1 to STD-02.3 (P06) apply to the OCPP. Procedures PRC-02.1 to PRC-02.4 cover provisioning, certification, privileged access, and break-glass access.

Workforce accounts for order management, the storefront admin console, store controllers, and the payment switch are provisioned by identity governance from HR events and role templates approved by the system owner. Gap: about 180 acquired-banner (AB) pickers and managers received order management and handheld accounts in 2026-04 through a manual request from the legacy directory; 2 of 60 sampled terminations were disabled 3 and 5 business days late, both at AB stores (POAM-007).
evidence: Identity governance role templates; order management user export; P07 AC-2 results

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Joiner, mover, and leaver events flow automatically from the HR system to identity governance, which provisions and removes OCPP roles through SSO connectors.

SSO accounts inactive for 60 days are disabled by identity governance. Gap: POS operator IDs (cashier and manager override IDs) are managed in the POS back office, not in identity governance; 1,140 POS operator IDs inactive more than 90 days were still enabled at assessment (POAM-015).
evidence: Identity governance inactivity job report; POS operator ID export

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Account creation, modification, disabling, and removal are logged by identity governance and forwarded to the SIEM.

Role-based access is enforced in order management (picker, store lead, customer care, administrator), the storefront admin console (content, merchandising, release manager), the POS back office (cashier, lead, manager, administrator), and the payment switch console (operator, administrator, auditor read-only).
evidence: Role matrix v7; access test results

implementation_statement: Information flow from lanes to store controllers to the payment switch is restricted by store payment VLAN access lists and colocation firewalls; e-commerce services reach the processor only through egress allow-lists in the Cloud A landing zone.

Duties are separated for switch configuration (administrators), routing table approval (Vice President, Payments delegate), and log review (SOC). Storefront release managers cannot approve their own payment page changes.
evidence: Separation of duties matrix; change approvals

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Least privilege is enforced through role templates. Administrative access to store controllers, the payment switch, and production containers is brokered just in time through PAM with session recording.
evidence: PAM policy export; quarterly CDE access certification

implementation_statement: Security functions (routing tables, key exchange settings, audit settings) are limited to switch administrators through PAM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Administrators use separate non-privileged accounts for email and web browsing; privileged accounts are vaulted in PAM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Use of privileged functions is logged by PAM session recording and sent to the SIEM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: SSO locks accounts for 30 minutes after 10 failed attempts; POS operator IDs lock after 6 failed attempts and require a lead reset.
Administrative consoles (order management, storefront admin, POS back office, payment switch) display the approved system use notification.
Back-office PCs and administrator laptops lock after 15 minutes; registers lock when the cashier signs off or after 10 minutes idle.
Administrative web sessions end after 15 minutes idle; customer sessions on the storefront end after 30 minutes idle on checkout pages.

Workforce and POS vendor remote access uses the zero-trust access service with MFA and PAM session recording. Gap: two refrigeration vendors keep always-on remote access tools on store controllers outside OCPP but on the same store network, segmented from the payment VLAN only by store firewall rules (POAM-004).
evidence: Zero-trust access logs; remote tool scan

implementation_statement: Store wireless uses WPA3-Enterprise with certificate authentication for handhelds; guest Wi-Fi is internet-only; the payment VLAN carries no wireless; quarterly rogue access point scans run at every store.
Use of external systems is governed by POL-05 and STD-05.2. Personal devices cannot reach OCPP administrative consoles.
Awareness and training policy (POL-05) and training standard STD-05.1 apply.
Annual security awareness training (97% completion in 2026), monthly phishing simulations for workforce with email, and skimmer and PIN pad tampering awareness for every cashier at hire and annually.
Role-based training: developers complete secure coding training annually; switch administrators and store technology staff complete PCI DSS role training.
Audit logging standard STD-01.4 applies (event types, retention, review).

Logged events include user access to cardholder data functions, administrative actions, access to audit logs, invalid access attempts, changes to authentication and accounts, log initialization and stopping, and creation or deletion of system-level objects on store controllers, the payment switch, and e-commerce services.
Audit records include user or process ID, event type, date and time, success or failure, origin, and affected component or resource.
Switch records also carry terminal ID, store ID, and response code (never full card data).

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: The SIEM alerts the SOC when a log source stops reporting for 60 minutes; failures of critical security controls are alerted and tracked.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews OCPP security events daily through automated SIEM correlation and 24x7 alerting. Gaps: change logs from the content delivery network and the tag manager that serve the express checkout and cart pages are not ingested (POAM-002); events from AB order management users are reviewed, but AB store systems that those users also use are not in the SIEM (POAM-009).
evidence: SIEM use case list; daily review records

implementation_statement: Audit review uses automated SIEM correlation and case management.
POS, switch, e-commerce, identity, PAM, and network logs are correlated in the SIEM.
All OCPP components synchronize time to designated internal time servers that use trusted external sources.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Logs are stored in a write-once central archive in a separate log account; only the SOC has read access and no one can delete within retention.
Audit records are kept at least 12 months, with the most recent 3 months immediately available in the SIEM.
Store controllers, the switch, containers, and administrative consoles generate the AU-2 events; forwarding is verified monthly against the SIEM source list.
Assessment and authorization standard STD-01.2 applies.
Controls are assessed annually by Internal Audit (2026-07-13 to 2026-08-28, P07) and by the QSA for the ROC (2026-10-19 to 2026-11-20).
Internal Audit reports to the audit committee and does not design or operate the controls it assesses; the QSA is an external independent assessor.
evidence: Internal Audit charter; QSA engagement letter

implementation_statement: Interconnection terms exist with the primary processor (merchant and processing agreements), each state EBT processor (retailer agreement and third party processor certification), and the delivery providers.
The POA&M is maintained in the GRC platform (P07 poam.csv) and reviewed monthly by the payments security council.
The CFO is the authorizing official equivalent; operation was authorized 2026-09-14 with conditions (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring: weekly vulnerability and configuration dashboards, monthly PCI DSS control metrics, quarterly reporting to the payments security council, and annual ROC.
Internal connections between store controllers, lanes, and PIN pads are documented in the store payment network standard and verified in the annual segmentation test.
Configuration and change management standard STD-01.5 and procedure PRC-01.3 apply.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Golden images for registers and store controllers, the switch server baseline, and container base images are version-controlled; cloud baselines are enforced by landing zone guardrails.

control_name: Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency
provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Drift is detected by cloud posture management and by the store configuration management tool.

Changes go through the change advisory board with risk rating, testing, and approval; payment page changes need the payment page owner approval. Gap: 3 of 40 sampled payment switch changes were emergency changes without the required post-implementation approval within 2 business days (POAM-012).

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: POS releases are tested in the lab store and a pilot of 3 stores before the staged rollout.
Security impact analysis, including PCI DSS scope impact, is part of each change request.
Only administrators through PAM can change store controller, switch, or production configurations; e-commerce changes deploy only through the CI/CD pipeline.

Hardening baselines apply to registers, store controllers, the switch, and containers. Gap: 3 of 25 sampled store controllers had the local firewall disabled after a POS vendor support session (POAM-013).
evidence: Configuration compliance report; P07 CM-6 results

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Only needed services and ports are enabled; application allow-listing on store controllers and registers.
Enabled services and ports are reviewed every 6 months against the baseline.

Cloud components are inventoried from tags; store controllers and registers from the store configuration management tool. Gap: 41 of about 2,780 PIN pads in the PIN pad inventory could not be matched to a store lane at reconciliation (POAM-014).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Inventory updates on install and removal through automated discovery.
Contingency and disaster recovery standard STD-03.3 applies.

The OCPP contingency plan covers roles, store-and-forward, payment switch failover, e-commerce regional failover, and restoration order (P05 BP-01, BP-02, BP-03). Gap: no procedure for a primary processor outage longer than the 4-hour store-and-forward window (POAM-016).
The plan is coordinated with the enterprise DR plan, the processor, state EBT processors, and store downtime procedures.
Essential functions (checkout with cash and store-and-forward; manual EBT vouchers) resume within 1 hour at every store.
Front-end leads complete annual downtime training, including manual EBT voucher procedures.
Switch failover and e-commerce regional failover are tested annually. Gap: the 2026-05-09 failover test did not include SNAP EBT routing, and manual voucher drills covered 3 of 112 stores (POAM-011).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Backups are stored in separate backup accounts and regions, with a weekly copy to COLO-2.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: E-commerce runs a warm standby in a second Cloud A region; the switch runs active-active in COLO-1 and COLO-2.
Two carriers and cellular failover at every store; diverse carriers at both colocation sites.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Order database log shipping every 15 minutes; daily immutable snapshots retained 35 days; switch configuration backed up after every change.
Quarterly restore tests verify order database integrity and counts.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Backups are encrypted with keys held in the backup account.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Recovery to a known state is documented for the switch, store controllers, and e-commerce. Gap: recovery of SNAP EBT routing after failover has never been demonstrated (POAM-011).
Store-and-forward queues are replayed to the processor after recovery with duplicate checks.
Identification and authentication standard STD-02.2 applies.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Workforce users authenticate to OCPP consoles through SSO with unique accounts; cashiers use unique POS operator IDs.
evidence: SSO configuration; POS operator ID policy

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Privileged access requires phishing-resistant MFA through PAM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: MFA is required for all non-console access into the CDE and for all remote access.
PIN pads are paired to lanes by serial number and key; store controllers authenticate to the switch with device certificates.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Identifiers are assigned by identity governance and never reused; POS operator IDs are assigned by store leads from employee numbers.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Workforce authenticators follow STD-02.2; switch and store controller service account secrets are vaulted and rotated. Inherited gap from the store network (CCP-05): default vendor credentials on ESL base stations at 3 of 12 sampled stores (found in P07; POAM-006).
evidence: PAM vault report; P07 IA-5 results

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Passwords are at least 12 characters and checked against a banned-password list.
Customers are uniquely identified in the storefront; bot detection and rate limits protect sign-in; saved-card changes need a one-time code.
POL-03 and the P08 runbooks apply.
Incident responders train annually; store technology and e-commerce on-call staff train on skimming and POS compromise.

The incident response plan is tested annually. Gap: the 2026-03-19 enterprise tabletop covered ransomware only; no exercise has covered a card data compromise or included the disclosure committee (POAM-010).
The SOC runs incident handling for the OCPP per P08. Gap: incidents at AB stores, whose staff use OCPP order management, are handled locally without SOC cases (POAM-009).
Incidents are tracked in case management.
Workforce report suspected incidents through the service desk; cashiers report suspicious PIN pads to the store lead and the SOC; acquirer notice follows the merchant agreement term (P08).
Enterprise incident response plan and runbooks (P08). Gap: the materiality playbook does not link card brand, acquirer, and forensic investigation steps to the disclosure timeline (POAM-010).
Maintenance standard STD-01.6 applies.
Register, PIN pad, and store controller maintenance is recorded in the store service system; PIN pad swaps require inventory updates.

Nonlocal maintenance of store controllers and the switch is through PAM with recording. Gap: two refrigeration vendors maintain store OT through always-on tools on the shared store network (POAM-004).
POL-04 and media standard STD-04.2 apply.
Retired store controllers and register drives are wiped and destroyed by a certified vendor with certificates; PIN pads are returned to the key injection facility.
Physical security standard STD-01.7 applies to stores, DCs, and colocation cages.
Colocation cage access lists are reviewed quarterly; store back offices with controllers are restricted to managers.
Colocation sites use badge plus biometric entry and escorted visitors; store controllers sit in locked back-office cabinets.
Planning standard applies; SSPs are required for tier-1 systems.
This SSP, reviewed annually and after major changes.
Workforce acknowledge POL-05 annually.
Moderate baseline selected, with High-baseline availability and testing supplements (SSP section 6).
Tailoring decisions are recorded in this file and SSP section 6.
Personnel security standard applies.
Background checks before hire for all staff with access to the CDE, within the limits of local law.
Core terminations disable SSO the same business day. Gap: AB terminations are processed in the legacy HR system and keyed manually; 2 of 60 sampled terminations were late (POAM-007).
Sanctions procedure PRC-01.1.
Risk assessment standard aligned to NIST SP 800-30 and IR 8286 Rev. 1.
The OCPP is categorized Moderate (SSP section 6).

System risk assessment 2026-06 to 2026-07 rolled into the enterprise register (P01); targeted risk analyses document the frequency of PCI DSS activities that allow flexibility. Gap: targeted risk analyses were missing for 3 of 11 requirements that need one, including the payment page check frequency for the express checkout (POAM-018).
Supply chain risks for the POS vendor, switch vendor, PIN pad supplier, and key injection facility are assessed in the vendor program.

Authenticated internal scans quarterly and after significant changes; external scans by an Approved Scanning Vendor quarterly. Gap: 4 high-risk vulnerabilities on store controllers were open past the 30-day remediation target at assessment (POAM-013).
Findings are treated through the POA&M and risk register.
Critical components: payment switch, store controllers, PIN pads, checkout service, and the hosted payment field integration.
PCI DSS responsibility clauses and AOC delivery terms are in POS, switch, processor, and hosting contracts.
External services are tiered and reviewed. Gap: of 71 TPSPs, 9 had an expired or missing AOC and 14 had no written responsibility matrix (POAM-003).
Code review and automated static and dynamic testing in the pipeline for bespoke e-commerce code before release.
No unsupported components in the OCPP; POS operating system end-of-support is tracked 24 months ahead.
System and communications protection standard applies.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: DDoS protection and a web application firewall front the storefront and APIs.

Store payment VLANs are separated from back-office, OT, and guest networks by store firewalls; the switch sits in a dedicated colocation segment. Gaps inherited from the store network: NAC at 61 of 98 core stores, and refrigeration and ESL controllers share the back-office VLAN at 37 stores (POAM-005).

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Deny-by-default network policies in both clouds and at store firewalls.
Card data is encrypted at the PIN pad; store-to-switch and switch-to-processor links use TLS 1.2 or higher; the web checkout uses TLS 1.2 or higher.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Keys for tokens and storage are managed in the landing zone key service; PIN pad keys are injected by the key injection facility and the company holds no decryption keys.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Validated cryptographic modules per the provider attestation; strong cryptography per STD-04.1.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Order and token databases are encrypted with customer-managed keys; no full card numbers are stored.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Cryptographic protection at rest for OCPP data and backups.
System integrity standard applies.
Critical patches within 30 days; POS releases staged monthly. Gap: 4 high-risk vulnerabilities on store controllers open past target (POAM-013).
EDR on store controllers, back-office PCs, and switch servers; registers run allow-listing.

24x7 SOC monitoring, intrusion detection at colocation and cloud boundaries, and change detection on the main web checkout. Gap: stores without NAC cannot detect rogue devices on the store network (POAM-005).
Inbound and outbound traffic at colocation and cloud boundaries is monitored for unusual patterns, including connections from store controllers to unknown destinations.
Threat intelligence includes retail and payment advisories; alerts are triaged by the SOC.

File integrity monitoring on store controllers and switch servers; payment page script inventory, integrity values, and change and tamper detection on the main web checkout. Gap: the express checkout and the cart pages that host retail media tags are not covered, and the tag manager can still inject scripts there (POAM-002).
Integrity checks of POS and switch software at startup and weekly; payment page checks at least weekly per the targeted risk analysis. Gap: no checks on express checkout pages (POAM-002).
Integrity violations raise SOC cases and page the e-commerce on-call engineer.
Input validation on checkout and order APIs; switch message validation rejects malformed ISO 8583 messages.
Retention follows the records schedule: no sensitive authentication data after authorization; truncated card numbers only on receipts and reports.
Supplier tiering and contract controls for POS, PIN pad, and switch suppliers.
Annual assessment of tier-1 suppliers and TPSP AOC review. Gap: 9 TPSP AOCs expired or missing (POAM-003).

Annual external and internal penetration tests of the CDE, and segmentation tests at least every 12 months, by a qualified internal team independent of the system teams. Gap: the 2026 application penetration test (2026-01) did not cover the express checkout released in 2026-02 (POAM-002).
evidence: 2026 penetration test report; segmentation test report

implementation_statement: Capacity planning for peak holiday and emergency-preparation volume (hurricane watches) across switch, processor links, and checkout services. Planned for 2027 Q1 after the 2026 holiday peak test.
Continue essential payment functions during a processor outage longer than 4 hours (offline limits, cash logistics, customer messaging). Planned with POAM-016.

control_name: Recovery Time and Recovery Point Objectives

implementation_statement: Alternate storage is configured to meet the RTO and RPO in P05 (switch configuration and order database).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: The alternate colocation site is kept ready to carry full load (active-active).
Require primary and alternate telecommunications providers to share their contingency plans and test results. Planned at carrier contract renewals in 2027.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-03 Cloud landing zones (Cloud A and B)
implementation_statement: Switch software, routing tables, and store images are stored in a separate immutable backup account.
Restore store controllers within 1 hour from configuration-controlled golden images. Planned for 2027 Q2 (image distribution service).
